what_happened: The job "Add auditor and warden roles per the 2026-10-16 BRIEF addendum" (20261016-052605-qw38) ended failed. The producer stage reached its fixed 1800-second deadline before it finished, so the job stopped with no result. The event lists no acceptance criteria, blocker or major findings, or failed checks. Nothing was delivered. The work is a code change that adds two new roles. It is larger than a prompt edit, but it was still run as one producer stage with a single time limit.
cause: The producer runs as one stage with a fixed wall-clock deadline. Nothing estimates the size of the job against that deadline, splits a multi-part request into smaller pieces, saves partial progress, or shows progress to the operator. When the limit is hit, the stage fails and everything it did is lost. A request that adds several roles from a brief addendum is not split before it runs, so a stage that cannot finish in time is not found until the full 1800 seconds are spent. The registry class names "small, well-bounded" jobs, but this one is a multi-part code change. So the root cause is wider than small jobs: the deadline is not tied to the job's size, and no checkpoint or resume exists.
prevention: Change the producer stage so a deadline does not discard its work. (1) The producer commits checkpoints and writes a progress note as it goes. (2) On deadline, the job keeps the partial result and is marked "timed out, resumable", which is separate from a real failure. A retry then continues from the checkpoint. (3) Planning splits a request that adds several roles into one item per role, each with its own deadline. (4) The deadline is set from the size of the job's plan, not one fixed value.
proposed_request: Make a producer-stage timeout keep its work and be resumable. Outcome: when a producer stage reaches its deadline, the job is recorded as "timed out" and not as a plain failure. The worktree changes made so far and a short progress note are kept. Retrying the job resumes from them, not from nothing. Also, when planning sees a request that adds several separate parts (for example two new roles), it splits the request into one plan item per part, each with its own deadline. Acceptance: (1) a test with a stub producer that exceeds the deadline shows the partial changes are kept and the job state is "timed out"; (2) a retry of that job starts from the kept changes; (3) a request naming two roles produces two plan items; (4) the existing gate commands (cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets, cargo fmt --check) pass. After that, re-run the job "Add auditor and warden roles per the 2026-10-16 BRIEF addendum" (20261016-052605-qw38).
